stories.headline: Third drone strike in a week shuts down Yandex data centre in Vladimir
stories.script: In our lead story today, The fight over AI infrastructure has become a front line. Drones hit a Yandex data centre in Vladimir, east of Moscow, overnight into Sunday, and the company said operations there were completely suspended, with no injuries reported and several services down. It is the third strike on Yandex sites in a week, after Sasovo on Thursday, which houses two of the three supercomputers Yandex uses to develop its AI model, and Kaluga on Friday. Yandex, often called Russia's Google, told customers to switch on disaster-recovery plans and warned that its remaining setup was unstable. Kyiv says it is targeting sources of revenue for Moscow's war effort, and Russia has hit Ukrainian data centres and telecoms sites over the past month.
stories.whyThisMatters: Critical development shaping WORLD artificial intelligence policy and sovereign compute.
keyPoints: Third drone strike in a week shuts down Yandex data centre in Vladimir
Al Jazeera

stories.headline: Trump administration leans on liability law to police AI models that go rogue
stories.script: Turning to the United States, Washington's AI safety plan is shaping up as report it, or be liable for it. A Bloomberg analysis published over the weekend lays out how the Trump administration is leaning on existing liability law instead of new rules. The White House's new Super Intelligence Force, led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, warned developers after Anthropic disclosed that its models had acted on real websites that companies must immediately disclose incidents involving their models, and that delayed notification will not be tolerated. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and former AI czar David Sacks back making developers pay for harm, and the FTC is already questioning OpenAI, Anthropic and others about product safety.
stories.whyThisMatters: Critical development shaping USA artificial intelligence policy and sovereign compute.
keyPoints: Trump administration leans on liability law to police AI models that go rogue
The Japan Times (Bloomberg)

stories.headline: Nvidia in talks to deepen its investment in Reflection AI or buy the open-weight model startup
stories.script: In concurrent industry updates, Nvidia is in early discussions about acquiring or increasing its investment in Reflection AI, which develops open-weight AI models, the Financial Times reported. Reflection was last valued at approximately 25 billion dollars, and several possible deal structures are under consideration, including an arrangement in which Nvidia would hire staff and license technology rather than buy the company outright. No agreement has been announced, and the talks could still fall apart. Nvidia has already invested 800 million dollars in the startup, and a deal would deepen its position beyond chips into the models built around its hardware.
stories.whyThisMatters: Critical development shaping USA artificial intelligence policy and sovereign compute.
keyPoints: Nvidia in talks to deepen its investment in Reflection AI or buy the open-weight
Reuters

stories.headline: Shing-Tung Yau launches mathematics and AI lab alliance of more than 1,000 Chinese mathematicians
stories.script: Meanwhile in China, China's top mathematicians are teaming up around AI. Fields medallist Shing-Tung Yau launched the Yau Laboratory Alliance for Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence at Tsinghua University on Sunday, linking eight institutions and more than 1,000 mathematicians in Beijing, Shanghai, Nanjing, Shenzhen and Hong Kong. Its six priorities include maths-specific AI models, open infrastructure for AI-assisted research, using maths to make AI more interpretable and secure, and a new journal for AI-assisted mathematics. Yau warned that China lags the US in using AI for frontier science, and said AI properly harnessed could be epoch-making but, poorly managed, could bring catastrophic consequences for China's science.

stories.headline: SK Square backs Japanese physical AI startup Mujin to expand into robotics
stories.script: In Asia, Korean chip money is moving into robot brains. SK Square, the investment arm of SK Group, owner of memory maker SK hynix, has joined the Series D round of Japanese physical AI company Mujin through its overseas unit TGC Square, Korean business press reported on Sunday. Mujin makes MujinOS, software that lets industrial robots plan and carry out work in factories and warehouses, and SK wants to use it in its chip-making and logistics lines. SK Square's stake was not disclosed. It is the eighth AI or chip startup in the US and Japan that SK Square has backed.
stories.whyThisMatters: Critical development shaping ASIA artificial intelligence policy and sovereign compute.
keyPoints: SK Square backs Japanese physical AI startup Mujin to expand into robotics
KED Global

stories.headline: A quarter of India's workforce is highly exposed to AI, says study launched by Chief Economic Adviser
stories.script: Turning to India, About a quarter of India's workforce is now highly exposed to AI, according to a white paper from the Great Lakes Institute of Management's Centre for Finance and Economic Research in Chennai, launched by Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran on Sunday. The share of high-routine occupations has grown since 2012. Exposure is not the same as job loss: 7.6 percent of workers are positioned to gain productivity as AI complements their work, while 11.4 percent face potential displacement. Agriculture and skilled trades, which employ over 54 percent of the working population, show low substitution risk. The risk is sharpest for the young: 39.4 percent of workers aged 15 to 24 are in roles with high substitution risk, and for them high-routine jobs outnumber complementary roles by 7.6 to 1, against 4 to 1 for older workers.

stories.headline: Lancet assessment ranks malicious AI use and nuclear war as top threats to humanity by 2100
stories.script: In other global developments, Humans could become extinct by the year 2100 due to malicious use of AI or nuclear conflict, according to a new global risk assessment. They top a list of 17 major threats to human health over the next 75 years, which also includes cuts to aid spending by wealthy countries, the climate crisis and childhood malnutrition. The experts behind The Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health said all the threats interact, meaning they must be addressed together, but stressed that there was a realistic route to act on each.

keyPoints: Lancet assessment ranks malicious AI use and nuclear war as top threats to human

stories.headline: Microsoft's Satya Nadella says AI models need an emergency brake and minimal trust
stories.script: Turning to the United States, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says it is time to step back and assess the trust architecture of AI. In a lengthy post on X, he wrote that we cannot treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers and actions. He called for systems where models can be contained and observed and leave behind tamper-proof, human-readable evidence, and argued that the most trustworthy system will be the one that enables people to trust the model the least. Businesses, he suggested, should limit and monitor AI agents' access to sensitive systems and keep an emergency brake within reach.

stories.headline: Odyssey-3 world model and an AWS Nvidia toolchain add new building blocks for physical AI
stories.script: In enterprise infrastructure, Physical AI got two new building blocks. Odyssey opened a public research preview of Odyssey-3, a world model the company says can control robot arms and humanoids, drive a car, fly drones and play video games. A movement policy trained on about two hours of GTA V footage carried over to Red Dead Redemption 2 with no extra training. Its headline physics score of 66.1 came from the best of eight attempts per task, and the results are the company's own. Separately, AWS released an open-source Physical AI Toolchain built with Nvidia that links data collection, training, simulation, validation and deployment on robots. It draws on Amazon's own fleet of more than a million robots and plugs in Nvidia's Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, GR00T and Cosmos tools.

stories.headline: Context Language Models let AI agents rewrite their own working memory
stories.script: In another major development, What if a model decided for itself what to remember? Researchers from Meta, MIT and the University of Washington describe Context Language Models, which treat their working memory as a file they can freely rewrite, keeping key facts, deleting dead ends and writing their own progress notes, instead of relying on fixed summarising or retrieval rules. With no extra training, they reported 11.4 percent higher accuracy with 21.5 percent less compute on the BrowseComp-Plus research benchmark, and 5 percent better scores with 59 percent less compute on a 12-hour task suite. Reinforcement learning lifted Qwen3.5-9B on BrowseComp-Plus from 28.8 percent to 42.5 percent. The authors flag real risks: a model can throw away something it later needs, and an editable memory gives prompt injections a place to hide.

keyPoints: Context Language Models let AI agents rewrite their own working memory

stories.headline: Sequoia-backed chip startup Nuvacore raising funds at about a 2.5 billion dollar valuation
stories.script: In concurrent industry updates, Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly 2.5 billion dollar valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising. Nuvacore is seeking the funds as appetite for central processors has swollen with the demand for data-crunching capacity to power chatbots. CPUs perform vital functions as traffic controllers for Nvidia's AI chips and run autonomous AI software known as agents.

keyPoints: Sequoia-backed chip startup Nuvacore raising funds at about a 2.5 billion dollar

stories.headline: AI's independent safety evaluators step into the spotlight
stories.script: Expanding on regulatory scrutiny, Two months ago, independent evaluators occupied a relatively sleepy corner of the multitrillion-dollar artificial intelligence industry. Now they are being asked to come to its rescue. While Anthropic and OpenAI are at the heart of a fierce debate over whether they can safeguard their advanced models and grow their businesses at the same time, they are seeking support from a handful of small third-party groups such as Model Evaluation and Threat Research, Apollo Research and Transluce.
stories.whyThisMatters: Critical development shaping USA artificial intelligence policy and sovereign compute.
keyPoints: AI's independent safety evaluators step into the spotlight

stories.headline: Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in scheme to divert Nvidia AI servers to China
stories.script: Meanwhile in China, A contractor linked to Super Micro Computer has pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export computer servers containing advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, according to a court filing on Friday. In March, US prosecutors charged Ting-Wei Willy Sun and two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder, with conspiring to divert about 2.5 billion dollars worth of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws. The court docket showed Sun entered his guilty plea on Thursday in US District Court in Manhattan.
stories.whyThisMatters: Critical development shaping CHINA artificial intelligence policy and sovereign compute.
keyPoints: Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in scheme to divert Nvidia AI servers to Ch

stories.headline: Japan's Sumitomo Bakelite expands chip packaging materials output in China and Singapore amid AI boom
stories.script: In Asia, The Tokyo-based company said on Friday that it would add production lines for mould underfill materials and compression-moulding granules at its facilities in Suzhou, in eastern China's Jiangsu province, and in Singapore. The company did not disclose an investment amount. The expansion is expected to roughly double its production capacity for mould underfill materials and triple that for compression-moulding granules, underscoring the growing importance of advanced packaging materials in the AI chip supply chain.

keyPoints: Japan's Sumitomo Bakelite expands chip packaging materials output in China and S

stories.headline: Google faces local backlash over its 15 billion dollar AI data centre in Visakhapatnam
stories.script: Turning to India, Handcuffs encircle Google's logo on one campaign poster, while another warns that people cannot drink data, as opposition mounts to the tech giant's planned AI mega-facility in India. Excavators have swung into action, clearing forest and farmland on the southeast coast for the 15 billion dollar construction of Google's largest data centre outside the United States. The project at Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, a port often called Vizag, is championed by India as a cornerstone of its technological ambitions.

keyPoints: Google faces local backlash over its 15 billion dollar AI data centre in Visakha
